content.user_title: Trace Root Causes in Debugging Workflows
content.value_statement: Deep failures often hide the original bad input or state change. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through backward tracing, instrumentation, and test bisection.
actual_capabilities: Guides backward tracing from a symptom to the original trigger.
Explains how to inspect call chains and passed values.
Shows where to add temporary stack trace instrumentation.
Includes a helper script for local test pollution bisection.
Recommends validation and defense layers after the source fix.
Provides examples for empty directory and test setup failures.
limitations: It needs logs, stack traces, or reproducible behavior to guide analysis.
The helper script assumes npm test and may need changes for other test runners.
It can run local tests repeatedly when the user invokes the script.
It does not replace security review for production data handling.

use_cases.title: Trace a Deep Runtime Failure
use_cases.description: Walk from the failing operation back through callers until the bad value or state change is found.

use_cases.title: Find a Test Polluter
use_cases.description: Use local bisection to identify which test creates unwanted files or shared state.

use_cases.title: Review a Regression Fix
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed fix addresses the source cause and adds useful boundary validation.

prompt_templates.title: Trace This Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner debugging with an error and stack trace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace this failure from the symptom to the likely source. Use the root-cause-tracing process and ask for missing logs if needed: [paste error and stack trace].

prompt_templates.title: Find the Bad Input
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging with a known wrong value.
prompt_templates.prompt: The wrong value is [value] at [function or file]. Trace backward through callers and identify where it first becomes wrong.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Instrumentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging when manual tracing is incomplete.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a temporary instrumentation plan for this failure. Include what to log, where to log it, and how to remove it after diagnosis.

prompt_templates.title: Design Test Bisection
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a test bisection workflow to find which test creates [file or state]. Include pre-checks, expected evidence, and cleanup precautions.

output_examples.input: A command fails because it runs in the repository root instead of a temporary directory.
output: Immediate cause: the operation received an empty working directory.
Trace target: find where that empty value entered the call chain.
Likely fix: validate the value during setup and at the operation boundary.

output_examples.input: A test suite leaves a hidden metadata directory in the source tree.
output: Start by checking whether the directory exists before tests run.
Run targeted test bisection in a clean workspace.
Inspect the first polluting test for shared setup or early access to temporary paths.

output_examples.input: A patch fixes the failure where it appears but not the caller chain.
output: The patch may hide the symptom without fixing the source cause.
Trace one level higher and inspect the value passed into the failing function.
Add validation after the source fix to prevent recurrence.

best_practices: Start at the symptom, then move one caller upward at a time.
Log stack traces before the operation that mutates state.
Fix the source cause, then add validation at later boundaries.
anti_patterns: Patching only the failing line without tracing the bad value.
Adding broad logging that exposes secrets or floods test output.
Running the helper script in a dirty workspace without checking existing pollution.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and includes a helper script, but execution requires an explicit user or agent action.

faq.question: What bugs fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It works best when the visible failure is far from the original bad input, setup mistake, or state mutation.

faq.question: Can it help with test pollution?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a bisection approach for finding which test creates unwanted files or shared state.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the error, stack trace, recent changes, reproduction steps, and any known wrong values.

faq.question: Does it only work with npm?
faq.answer: The included script uses npm test, but the tracing method can be adapted to other test runners.

faq.question: How should temporary instrumentation be handled?
faq.answer: Add focused logs near the risky operation, avoid secrets, and remove the instrumentation after diagnosis.
